title: How Building Actually Works in RuneScape Dragonwilds! Guide + Tips!
author: Kodeations
description:
Struggling to make sense of the building system in RuneScape Dragonwilds? This guide breaks down the entire building system in Dragonwilds clearly, simply, and with context. We go over snapping, ghost mode, repair systems, elevation tricks, and more. It’s not “secret knowledge,” just better explained. Great for new players, returning RuneScapers, and anyone who skipped the tutorial. Have a building trick I missed? Drop it in the comments below!

In this video, you'll learn:
- How to build efficiently using snapping & elevation
- How Ghost Mode and Eye of Oculus actually work
- How to repair, delete, and reposition structures properly
- Smart tips for temporary bases and surviving warband raids

transcript.text: All right, so starting us off with the basics here. If you press B on your keyboard, it will open up the building
menu. Obviously, at the top, you've got all of your individual tabs for all your building pieces and materials. Now, I
might have more listed on here than you do if you guys are just starting off in the game, or heck, you could be playing
for hours and have never really uncovered this, but essentially, as you play through the game and progress and
find blueprints, you will then uncover new recipes that you can craft. Whether it's decorations, whether it's building
pieces, tier one, tier 2, you name it. You can go ahead and select an item and then obviously hover over wherever you
want to place that item and it will turn green if you can place it. It will turn red if you can't place it. And if you
try to place something that you can't, you'll hear this noise. And that essentially just means
you can't place the item where you're trying to place it. Even if it might look like the item is green and not red,
because that does sometimes happen. and I've had that randomly happen, especially when you're fine-tuning or
putting decorations in a small little area inside of your base. But anyways, here you're going to go ahead and press
the left mouse button in order to place that item down. And that's essentially how you would build items. Now,
obviously, if you decide later on, let's say we've placed this foundation, and we no longer want this foundation here.
What you can do is you can press B on your keyboard, it does not matter what you select in the building menu. So, for
instance, we're going to select these stairs, and let's say we want to delete uh the first foundation. We're going to
go ahead and highlight over it. Make sure it's there. And we're going to press the middle mouse button.
Basically, the little scroll wheel if you have one. That's what you're going to press in like a button. Not scroll
it, but press it in and then it will delete whatever that item is. Also, in Runescape, it's important to note that
so far I've been receiving a 100% of my materials back for destroying an item. This is really, really handy to know
when it comes to placing temporary structures out in the world. If you're going to be placing something down,
maybe to just sleep really quick, don't worry about it or worry about using the resources because you can just break it
all down after you're done sleeping and then get those resources back. With that being said, we're going to go back into
the building menu here and let's talk about a couple of other things. First one, let's say you want to place this
foundation right here, but you don't want to be this high level, right? Elevation. You actually want to lower it
down. If you press and hold the control option as the game tells you here, you can actually scroll your middle mouse
wheel up or down and it will bring that foundation all the way down. You can sink it into the ground. You can raise
it all the way up, even to the point where it is considered unstable and you can't place it. But it really allows you
to fine-tune where you want to place that item. Same thing goes for if you hold the alt option. If you press and
hold alt and then scroll your wheel, it will bring the item closer to you or away from your character. So again, just
a really, really awesome quality of life feature here to allow you to fine-tune and place your items exactly where you
want them. And now lastly here, when it comes to the basics, we also have snap points. You can see the basic four snap
points on the foundation that I just placed. They're indicated here with the uh the white little dots on the the one
I just placed. And then you can see the ones on the new one that is currently in red. You can see the um yellow little
circles on top of the of the red. that essentially will tell you what snap points are currently available for those
pieces. If you press Y on your keyboard, as you can see in the bottom right hand side, that will actually give you an
additional three snapping points on each side of your item. Lastly, if you press Y one more time, it basically gets rid
of all the snapping points and allows you to freely place building items. Again, this really allows for a lot of
customization when it comes to placing items inside of items. As you can see here, this foundation underneath the
other foundation, you can lower it, raise it, do all of those things without having to, you know, it be really
finicky about randomly jumping from the place you want to place it to the snapping point. Now, moving on to some
other things here. Let's talk about in the building menu. You actually have two other modes that are kind of hidden off
to the left hand side of your building screen. The first one up is going to be T on your keyboard or essentially the
repair mode. If you go ahead and click click the repair mode, if you have the items necessary in your inventory, you
can repair the items by walking up to them. You can see the little wrench icon and the pin icon in the center of your
screen. If you go ahead and see that, you can see we can press the leftclick option to repair the item. By pressing
the left click, it will go ahead and repair it. And then you can also see and check what exactly the health amount is
of that specific building piece. So, you can see that if I look at the foundation, it says 100%, but if I look
at the stairs, it says 74%. And it tells you, it tells me I'm going to need one ashwood log. I'm going to go ahead and
click on that, and then it will instantly repair that piece. And then the second option below the repair mode
brings us to the ghost mode. Now, if you go ahead and click on ghost mode, what essentially this is going to do is allow
you to blueprint out your base build without actually using the materials or placing those specific items. So to give
you an example here, let's say we want to add on to my base, but we don't want to use the necessary resources. We're
going to go ahead and select the foundation for instance. Make sure our snapping is turned on. As you saw, my
snapping was turned off. But let's say I'm just going to want to add this go going all the way across. And as you can
see, I leave the building menu by pressing B. Now you can see I have this blueprint. These items were not consumed
to place it, but it allows you to essentially plan out whatever the build is that you desire without having to use
the resources or even having those resources on hand in order to build them. And what's really cool about this
is number one, obviously, if you have friends building with you or on the server playing with you, they can also
see your hologrammed out blueprint and then continue to build it exactly how you want it. they can contribute the
resources if they have them in their inventory to continue the building pieces. And then the second thing that's
really cool is you can also place the items that you do have in your inventory if you do not have all of the required
ones. So to give you an example, if I go back here to my building menu and let's
say I'm going to place the tier 2 of the floors. So let's say I'm going to go ahead and place the tier 2 floor here.
You can see I've got four out of the, you know, two different materials that are required. I can go ahead and press E
on them and it will go ahead and take those items from my inventory, place them into this, you know, hologram
blueprint build. Um, but it will obviously not build it because I still need those two remaining resources. But
again, it's just a really cool quality of life feature here that allows you to put in the materials that you do
currently have and then it'll basically sit there and wait until you do have the
remaining materials to continue building it out. Additionally, it's important to note that in Runescape Dragon Wilds,
there's also a structure support system. So if we go ahead and place this large uh support beam for instance and we go
ahead and place it uh on the next one all the way up right we can see the individual snap points that we have
available. But if we go ahead and place it uh the higher that we place the item the less support that that item will
have. So eventually as we place more and more items, for instance, if we go ahead
and place a flat uh floor for instance, we can see that now this item, which used to be green, is now yellow, right?
Eventually that item will turn red. As you can see here, it is currently unstable and it will not allow you to
place that item any further without providing additional support. And then moving on to another really awesome
quality of life feature that they've added in the game brings us to the skills. As you level up from doing
different activities in the game, one of them is called the construction tab. Now, for obviously building things, as
it says here, build new structures to level this skill, you will unlock additional, you know, abilities to use.
And at level 11, really early on in the game, you unlock the ability of the eye of Oculus. What makes this a very handy
skill is that let's say you want to play something higher than your breach can go, right? So, in other games like Ark
Survival Ascended, you might have to do the little, you know, jump to place and time your jump, you know, exactly right
in order to place that specific item in that location. In Conan Exiles, you might have to climb up a wall and
hopefully you got enough stamina in order to place the item where you want. You name it. Well, this game does a
really good job of fixing all of that. What you can do is you can actually press and hold the skills button on the
screen, which essentially is Q. It will then open up this menu here to allow you to use whatever skills you have on your
wheel. Down at the bottom, I've got Eye of Oculus. It is going to cost you three of the runes. You go ahead and use it,
and your character will actually sit in place. And what will now happen is it will give you the ability to actually
select a building item. So, let's say we want to place this vertical thick beam for whatever reason. We can go ahead and
now, as you can see, have a free movement character. You can see that we can move all the way around. There is a
radius, right? You can you can only go so far away from your individual character, but it does allow you to
actually place and build wherever you want. We can essentially keep on placing here. There you go. That's another
example of the structure. You can see we can't place this third one because it's too high. We went from green to yellow
now to red. Um, but yeah, you can essentially build whatever you want wherever you want and you don't have to,
you know, be bound to wherever your character's position actually is. And on top of freely placing the items, you can
also use the Oculus to go around and it will actually collect the items uh that your inventory can hold. And on top of
that, you can also go through objects. So that includes the individual foundation, you can go through crafting
benches, you can literally go through everything um while you were inside of this, you know, Oculus uh skill. So
again, really, really nice quality of life feature here that they've added in the game, and it definitely will take
your builds to the next level. Now, next up, I have some additional building tips I would like to mention in this video
that I think really do come in handy um when you're playing throughout the game. The first one, let's say you're on an
adventure and you need to sleep. Either you are exhausted in game or maybe it's nighttime and you want to skip the night
and you want to go directly to daytime. Well, you don't want to have to run all the way back to your base in order to do
so. What you can actually do is you can actually open up your building menu and one quick, easy, dirty way to do this is
actually place a single foundation. And then you can go ahead and place a couple of walls. Again, we're not looking to
build anything fancy here. We're just looking to place a couple of walls. And then we also need a roof. So, if we go
ahead and place one individual roof item, and then you can actually place a bed. So, going ahead and placing a bed
right here into the corner will actually allow you to go ahead and rest by just utilizing the one foundation, the two
walls, and then the actual roof. It doesn't have to be connected. It does not have to be a full closed shed. By
just placing it exactly as you see here on screen, it will allow you to rest anywhere and everywhere you are without
having to farm a bunch of resources or build a bunch of stuff because you're more than likely just going to delete it
right away as soon as you get done building it because you want to continue on your adventure. And now the next tip
brings us to the dragon's poison radius. It'll just randomly come and find you wherever you are in the world and start
dropping these big poison radius around you. Well, if you happen to be inside of your base or think that a base location
is going to be safe, well, that's not true here. It seems to be, at least at the current state of the game, as of
right now in its early access state, what approximately a week after its initial release, the poison radius can
still affect you inside of your base. So, it's a lot easier to avoid these poison circles by getting outside of
your base and running around. I wouldn't try to build specific structures or different layers of different structures
or even in different areas like a cave for instance because it does not seem to be, you know, safe whatsoever from these
poison radius. And the same thing goes for the warb band raids. What a lot of people don't know is that if you're
actually inside of your base, the enemies will attack your base. They will walk up to your building. They will
destroy the foundations, the doors, the walls, the crafting benches, even your bed, which there goes your respawn
point. you name it, they will destroy all of that stuff because their ultimate goal and objective is to get to you as
fast as they can to kill you. So, a really big tip is is once a war band starts, run outside. Get outside of your
base. They will not just randomly start attacking your base for no reason. So, get outside of your base, run around
outside, fight them on, take them off, you know, lead them one by one, whatever you got to do in order to prevent them
from doing damage to your base build. As long as you're not inside of the base, they seem to do a really good job of
leaving it alone and not affecting it whatsoever. If you love building in Runescape Dragon Wilds and you found
this guide helpful, you've got to check out the 10 tips that I wish I knew sooner video that you see here on
screen. As always, don't forget to like the video. Drop a comment down below if you have any additional building tips
here to add onto the video for people to check out. And don't forget to subscribe
here on the channel for more guides for Runescape Dragon Wilds.
